C-V1-OPENCODE-CONFIG-MIGRATION.Summary: Add host-gated automatic materialization of the legacy V1 OpenCode configuration into the native V2 shape inside `vvoc sync`, plus method-aware host guidance in `vvoc upgrade`, so upgrading a machine that runs an OpenCode v1 host with vvoc 1.7.0 requires only the user's own OpenCode 2.0.18 install.
C-V1-OPENCODE-CONFIG-MIGRATION.Problem: vvoc 2.x refuses V1-shaped OpenCode documents before any write, and the upgrade chain's post-install sync fails under an unsupported host, so users on OpenCode v1 and vvoc 1.7.0 must migrate `opencode.json` by hand. OpenCode V2 normalizes supported V1 configuration in memory but provides no materializing config-migration command, leaving the materialized file as a manual task.

Goals.Goal: When `sync` runs after the host is upgraded, materialize a clean native V2 `opencode.json(c)` from the existing V1 document, following the official V1-to-V2 migration guide mappings, with a timestamped backup and a validate-before-write guarantee.

Convert each nested agent, command, provider, model, and MCP entry wholly or not at all, never writing a partially converted nested entry, and abort without writing with a precise checklist when a field is unmappable or report-only.

Translate vvoc-specific role intent (`model`, `small_model`, and per-agent `model` values of the form `vv-role:*`) into the pinned vvoc plugin entry modelIntent envelope, and register the native `plugins` entry.
Make `vvoc upgrade` detect an unsupported host, print a best-effort method-aware next step, and exit non-zero with an explicit message that migration did not run.
Preserve unrelated settings and comments and keep repeated sync idempotent with no backup spam.

Constraints.Constraint: The migration runs only when the OpenCode host is inside the supported window; the host gate and the pinned runtime service version are not relaxed.
vvoc never installs, replaces, or uninstalls the OpenCode host, and no `--with-host` flag or standalone migration command is added.
Each nested agent, command, provider, model, and MCP entry is converted wholly or left alone; partial nested conversion is refused because OpenCode V2 forbids nested V1 and V2 mixing.

OpenCode's own terminal client migration from layered `tui.json(c)` to a single global `cli.json` is owned by OpenCode and is not reimplemented; `vvoc.json` v1/v2 upgrade is out of scope because 1.7.0 is already schema v3.
Config writes stay conservative, comment-preserving, and idempotent; invalid or unmappable documents fail before mutation.
Work is validated with isolated fixtures and does not migrate any live user configuration, publish, push, or bump the package version.

NonGoals.NonGoal: No standalone `vvoc migrate-to-v2` command, no `--with-host`, and no host installation or replacement.
No generation of V2 policies for `enabled_providers` or `disabled_providers`, and no conversion of accepted-but-unsupported fields, `lsp`, or ambiguous provider and model shapes.
No `vvoc.json` pre-v3 upgrade and no deletion or pruning of a legacy `tui.json(c)`.
No backup retention or rotation policy beyond one timestamped sibling backup per change, and no exhaustive install-manager or version-manager detection.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: AC-01: Given a captured vvoc 1.7.0 configuration set (`opencode.json`, `tui.json`, `vvoc.json`) and a host inside the supported window, `sync` produces a native-valid `opencode.json`, writes a timestamped sibling backup, and preserves comments and unrelated keys.

AC-02: Every documented mechanical mapping is applied: plugin to plugins with tuple-to-object conversion; agent and mode to agents with prompt to system, disable to disabled, variant joining, request-body moves, and maxSteps to steps; command to commands with subtask to subagent; skills object to array; snapshot to snapshots; attachment to media; reference to references; mcp servers with split timeouts and snake_case OAuth; compaction keep and buffer; permission plus tools to the ordered permissions array with action renames; provider shape and canonical IDs; provider model capability, cache, variant-array, and settings conversions; small_model to the title agent; autoshare to share; and autoupdate to update.
AC-03: A nested entry that cannot be converted wholly causes a no-write abort with a precise manual checklist, and no partially converted nested entry is ever written.

AC-04: Report-only fields (provider filters, accepted-but-unsupported fields, `lsp`, and ambiguous provider or model shapes) are listed for manual or agent-assisted action and never silently converted.

AC-05: vvoc role intent becomes the plugin modelIntent envelope, the native `plugins` entry is registered with legacy `/tui` specs deduplicated, and no `vv-role:*` value remains in a native config position.
AC-06: A transformed document that fails the pinned native codec causes a no-write abort with a non-zero exit, and the legacy `tui.json(c)` is reported but not deleted.
AC-07: A second `sync` on an already-migrated document changes nothing and creates no backup, and a host outside the supported window performs no config writes.

AC-08: `vvoc upgrade` under an unsupported host installs vvoc 2.x, prints a best-effort method-aware host next step (a single command when unambiguous, otherwise both documented install paths), and exits non-zero with an explicit message that migration did not run, replacing the current silent success on post-install sync failure.
AC-09: Existing `syncVvocConfig` behavior for a v3 config, including preserved retired and custom presets, is unchanged.

AC-10: Targeted migration, sync, and upgrade tests pass together with `bun run check`; module contracts, GRACE graph and verification, and README are synchronized where required; no generated `dist/` file is edited.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Fresh targeted test output for the migration, sync pre-step, and upgrade guidance; a native-valid migrated fixture with a timestamped backup; an idempotent second-run observation; a no-write abort observation for an unmappable fixture; and a passing `bun run check` on the final relevant snapshot.

Assumptions.Assumption: OpenCode V2 normalizes supported V1 configuration in memory without rewriting the source file, and the official V1-to-V2 migration guide mappings are authoritative for the native target shape.
Installing the pinned OpenCode 2.0.18 host replaces the legacy v1 `opencode` binary, so the host-first flow leaves no broken-v1 window; this is verified during planning and evidence collection.
A vvoc 1.7.0 `vvoc.json` is schema v3 and is already normalized by `syncVvocConfig`, including retired presets.
The post-install `vvoc sync` subprocess resolves the newly installed vvoc 2.x binary through PATH.
